title: Android 进程内存限制：memoryClass、largeHeap 与进程上限
key_conclusions: memoryClass and largeHeap primarily describe Java heap headroom, not total process PSS, Native Heap, Graphics, or shared-buffer limits.
largeHeap can hide Java heap pressure but does not reduce native, graphics, dma-buf, mmap, or system-wide low-memory pressure.
LMKD risk depends on process state, oom_score_adj, PSS/RSS, and system pressure, not only app-level heap limits.
OOM and kill triage must first classify Java Heap, Native Heap, Graphics/dma-buf, shared mappings, or system pressure.
shallow_points: The article does not include real memoryClass values from multiple devices.
It does not validate ActivityManager behavior and heap limit changes across Android versions and OEM configurations.
It does not include real LMKD kill logs or oom_score_adj samples.
It does not quantify largeHeap tradeoffs for startup, GC, LMKD risk, and system pressure.
